name: PT Dharma Satya Nusantara Tbk

frontmatter.title: Dharma Satya Nusantara: a planter priced for a palm-price fall, and an export channel that does not reach it
frontmatter.summary: GAPKI has raised its El Nino output-loss estimate to up to 3,000 kt with the worst in 2027, above the 2,200 kt the deck's next-year price rests on. The loss is national, so it supports the price leg; DSNG's own volume takes its nine-month fruit decline, about four per cent. BUY at Rp2,438, 93.6% from Rp1,285, about an eighth below the 10 November note on the peer reset and the volume cut.
thesis: The DCF enterprise value of IDR29.94tn is a first-forecast-year multiple: on next year's EBITDA of IDR5,114bn it is about six tenths of a turn above the 5.3x the cross-check applies, and further above the 4.1x the market pays, so the value rests on the cash-flow path rather than on a multiple [S3, S4].
At Rp1,285 the market discounts a palm price of US$1,086/t, below spot and well below the deck, so the disagreement is about the recovery and not about today [S0, S8].

Volume follows the company's plan this year at 637.0 kt and then carries its own nine-month fruit decline into FY2027E at 610.0 kt, about four per cent lower: the GAPKI loss is national and weighted to 2027, so the base takes DSNG's own trough rather than a pro-rata slice of the industry's, and the slice stays in the bear [S4, S5, S17, F35, F86].

The supply backdrop has tightened rather than eased: GAPKI now puts the El Nino loss at up to 3,000 kt with the worst in 2027, above the 2,200 kt the deck's next-year price was built on, so the recovery the market refuses to pay for has more support today than a week ago [S17, S8, F86, F37].
The levy-plus-freight wedge, not a proportional haircut, sets the realised price: a wider wedge takes the value to about nine tenths of the target and the return to five sixths of the base [S6, F36].

The index decision is a de-rating the palm price cannot offset: a one-point cost-of-equity premium takes the value to about nineteen twentieths of the target, and it is the first signpost we watch [S11].

catalysts.event: Revision to PP 24/2026 implementing the DSI single-intermediary channel, expected in mid-November; the tariff and price-range rules are still unfinalised
Monthly export duty and levy reset and the December reference price
DSI channel takes effect for coal, CPO and ferroalloy exports
First-quarter GAPKI production data, the first read on whether the El Nino loss reaches the upper bound the chairman gave at IPOC
Annual general meeting and dividend approval for the year to December

blocks.text: **What changed, and why.** On 12 November GAPKI's chairman told the industry's IPOC conference that El Nino could cost Indonesia up to 3,000 kt of palm output, heaviest in 2027, and asked for a stable policy framework [S17, F86]. That upper bound is above the 2,200 kt the deck's next-year price rested on [S8, F37], so the supply deficit behind our US$1,240/t benchmark is wider, not narrower. It is national: nine-month national output of 47,000 kt was still up 8.4% [S17, F87, F88]. DSNG's own volume takes its nine-month fruit decline, about four per cent in FY2027E [S5, F35], because the GAPKI loss is weighted to the year the company's own fruit is already falling; the pro-rata slice of the upper bound stays in the bear. The event itself moves no modelled input, but this version publishes about an eighth below the 10 November note for two other reasons: the cross-check multiples were reset to the liquid palm peers, and FY2027E volume now carries the company's own decline rather than the flat plan [S3, S4, S5].

The DSI channel is the outstanding policy question: from 1 January 2027 coal, crude palm oil and ferroalloy exports pass through PT Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI), which will set a fair export price range referenced to the HPE through a rulebook still to be written [S12, S13, S15]. For DSNG the direct reach is nil: the palm segment sold its entire nine-month line of IDR8,059.2bn domestically with nil export sales, and the export line is IDR977.3bn of wood products and shells, neither named in the announcement [S2, F61, F72, F75, F76]. What matters is the domestic parity price — the reference price less the export duty and levy — and it is unquantified because no tariff and no range formula exists [S6, S15, F36].

The view is BUY at a twelve-month value of Rp2,438, a total return of 93.6% from Rp1,285, of which 89.8% is price appreciation and the balance the next-twelve-month dividend. Volume follows the company plan this year and its own fruit decline next year, non-palm revenue is built from the segment accounts, the wider levy wedge sits in the bear and the index de-rating is sized separately [S3, S6, S11]. The DSI channel decides who files and at what range; the DHE SDA relaxation governs how much foreign currency an exporter may convert; neither changes volume, cost or the deck today [S9, S10, S12].

DSNG is an integrated oil-palm producer: 111,900 ha planted hectares, split between nucleus estates it owns and plasma blocks it develops for smallholders, with mills in East, Central and West Kalimantan; a wood-products business making engineered flooring and panels in Central Java; and a renewables business exporting palm-kernel shells and wood pellets to Japan and Korea [S4, S7, F38]. Last year CPO production reached 631 kt, sales 629 kt and the extraction rate 23.3% [S3, F1, F23, F26].

Almost all of the value is palm: the segment took 88.0% of nine-month revenue of 9,110 IDR bn, and the export line is almost entirely the other two segments [S2, F54, F31]. Strategy is unglamorous: replant older blocks, finish the plasma programme, delever, add small downstream projects such as a bio-CNG plant using mill effluent [S4, S7]. There is no large acquisition, so the capital question is whether dividend and replanting can both be funded from operating cash flow, and last year they were [S3, F50]. The company is controlled by the Triputra and Oetomo families, holding 30.6% and 29.2%, with an Oetomo family member as president director [S4, F55, F56]. It holds the estate through operating subsidiaries and a stake in an associated estate in East Kalimantan, with a small non-controlling interest, no dual-class structure and no share pledge [S2, S4].

The palm price is the largest driver. The house deck runs CPO from US$886/t in 2023 to US$1,007/t last year, US$1,135/t this year and US$1,240/t next, then fades to US$1,150/t long-run [S0]. The series is the World Bank Pink Sheet, whose annual averages for the three audited years are US$886/t in 2023, US$963/t in 2024 and US$1,007/t in 2025 [S16]. The deck's long-run marker sits above every print of those three years, so the terminal value is a premium to the observed average, not a haircut to spot [S16, S0]. Supply is tight and the estimate has tightened again: at IPOC on 12 November GAPKI's chairman put the El Nino loss at up to 3,000 kt, heaviest in 2027 and outlasting a single harvest, above the 2,200 kt the deck's next-year price rested on [S17, S8, F86, F37]. It has not appeared in the data yet: nine-month national output of 47,000 kt was up 8.4%, exports 27,300 kt and domestic use 18,800 kt under B50, so the projection is a 2027 event and the timing matters as much as the level [S17, F87, F88, F89, F90]. DSNG's own trough is earlier: nine-month fruit output 1,500 kt, CPO 451 kt [S5, F35, F34].

Policy is set monthly. The Ministry of Trade sets a reference price and derives the export duty and levy from it; for November the reference price is US$979/t and the combined charge US$246/t, down a fifth on October's US$308/t [S6, F36, F48, F77]. Because the charge is a dollar amount per tonne, not a proportional cut, the wedge shrinks as a ratio when the benchmark rises, which is what our realisation assumption carries [S6, S3]. The biodiesel mandate is the other pillar: the government confirmed the B50 blend, and palm use for biodiesel was 1,350 kt in August while exports rose and stocks fell [S6, F49]. No published formula sets the domestic price; it is negotiated against export parity, so a DSI charge or a binding range reaches a domestic seller through the same parity [S6, S12, S13]. GAPKI has asked that DSI stay an intermediary, warning that an unclear scheme adds cost [S14]. The conference carried the industry's policy ask too: the chairman said abrupt regulatory change and inconsistent signals disrupt investment planning, and asked for a predictable rulebook [S17] — a fair description of a file where the levy, the DSI rules and the DHE conversion have all moved inside a quarter [S6, S12, S15].

Competitive position is cost and certification, not share. DSNG is a small producer and a price taker, but its cash cost per tonne is set by its own estate and mill efficiency, with mills close to the fruit and an extraction rate above the industry average [S4, F26]. It has no pricing power, which is why it is valued on a through-cycle price rather than a multiple of one year's earnings [S3]. The market backdrop is a separate risk: MSCI is consulting on reclassifying Indonesia to standalone, which for a domestic mid-cap with a 33.1% free float is a de-rating with nothing to do with palm oil [S11, S0].

FY2026E against the company plan. The 2025 annual report prints its own 2026 projection as revenue flat, pre-tax profit up about a twentieth and equity up a tenth [S4]. Nine-month revenue was already ahead of the prior year [F31] and our FY2026E revenue of 12,781.6 is a shade above that run-rate: the difference is the reviewed deck for the fourth quarter, not a volume call, and this year is the only one where we sit above the printed plan. From FY2027E the model is below the plan on volume because the heaviest El Nino impact falls in the first forecast year beyond it [F86].

The last audited year is the anchor. Revenue was 12,315 IDR bn, cost of revenue 8,465 IDR bn and gross profit IDR3,850.0bn [S3, F5, F7]. Cost of revenue carries D&A of 974 IDR bn, which the data pack understated by an order of magnitude, so depreciation is restated to the audited note; on that basis EBITDA was IDR3,814.6bn at a margin of 31.0% [S3, F9].

Every EBITDA here is operating EBITDA: audited operating profit plus fixed-asset and right-of-use depreciation plus bearer-plant and intangible amortisation, the associate excluded and no add-back of the impairment or deduction of the biological gain [S3]. It sits a fraction of a per cent above operating profit of IDR2,829.4bn plus D&A of IDR973.7bn; the audited reconciliation prints IDR4,078.0bn, the difference being the associate's IDR168.4bn plus the IDR116.9bn impairment less the IDR10.4bn biological gain, stripped because the associate's profit cannot sit in the multiple while its book value sits in the bridge [S3, F52, F64-F67, F44].

After deducting the cost of non-palm revenue at a normal margin, the cash cost of a tonne of CPO is about IDR8.0m, or USD456 a tonne [S3, F7, F9]. That is well below the US$886.0 trough of the last three audited years and a fraction of the November reference price of US$979/t, so the estate is cash-positive at any observed price; we cannot source a global cost curve that carries DSNG, so we state the comparison rather than claim a quartile [S16, F79, F48]. The plantation is amortised over 20 years, and planted area of 111,900 ha over that life needs about five and a half thousand hectares of replanting a year, so the model carries capex of IDR1,066.9bn, above D&A of IDR1,011.2bn: replacement on the filing's own productive life, not a haircut [S3, F85, F38, F9, F11]. Costs are held at the last actual in real terms, inflated at the long-run rupiah anchor and terminal growth rate [S0, S3]. The plasma outlay is excluded: collections in the same investing section reimburse it [S3, F11].

Volume is the company's own plan. We carry 637.0 thousand tonnes, the printed 1.0% growth applied to the 631 kt produced last year, at a realised price of US$859.2 a tonne, revenue of IDR12,781.6bn, EBITDA of IDR3,997.4bn and earnings per share of Rp184.7 [S4, F60, F23, S3]. The nine-month outturn of 451 kt is below the prior year, so the plan needs a strong fourth quarter, and that risk sits in the bear volume leg [S5, F34]. The realisation ratio of 0.76 comes from the segment accounts and the deck's exchange rate [S2, F31, F34, S4].

Next year the deck does the work on price. The ratio is not held flat: the accounts show a dollar wedge between benchmark and realised price that behaves like a levy-plus-freight amount, so we hold the wedge and let the ratio rise with the benchmark [S2, S6, F36, F48]. Revenue reaches IDR13,973.7bn and EBITDA IDR5,113.6bn [S0, S3]. Volume takes the company's own trough: 610.0 kt against the 637.0 kt plan, about four per cent lower, the same rate as the nine-month fall in fruit output to 1,500 kt kt [S5, F35]. That is the most likely path rather than the cautious one: GAPKI's loss is weighted to 2027 [S17, F86], DSNG's fruit is already falling while the national crop still grew 8.4% [S17, F87, F88], and applying the national number to the plan would double-count a loss the crop data do not yet show. The pro-rata slice of the upper bound therefore stays the bear's volume leg, stacked on this base, and the recovery starts in FY2028E at 625.0 kt [S17, F86, F38].

The nine months are on the same basis: revenue 9,110 IDR bn and printed EBITDA 2,950 IDR bn, up about a per cent [S2, F31, F33], which on our definition is operating profit IDR2,113.5bn plus D&A IDR733.2bn, the printed line higher by the associate's IDR144.4bn and lower by the IDR41.4bn biological gain [S2, F68-F71]. Profit to owners was IDR1,465.0bn of total IDR1,441.7bn, and operating cash flow of 1,912 IDR bn fell as the prior year's working-capital release reversed [S2, F32, F78, F41].

The non-palm line is built, not escalated. Last year's non-CPO revenue of IDR3,216.9bn is palm kernel and kernel oil, wood and renewables [S3, F29]. Kernel scales with CPO volume; wood and renewables are held at the nine-month run-rate annualised, below last year because wood revenue and its margin fell, and no wood recovery is assumed, so a DHE-driven recovery is upside [S2, S9, S10]. The blended gross margin of 20.0% is a blend: kernel earns the palm-segment margin, wood a fifth of it [S3, S2].

The balance sheet is sound: forecast net debt at the year end of IDR2,433.8bn is under half of this year's EBITDA, against attributable equity of 11,481 IDR bn [S2, S3, F15], and the dividend at a payout of 27.1% and the replanting inside own capex are the claims on cash [S3, F21]. Accruals are negative in both fiscal years and in the nine months, and operating cash flow has exceeded net profit in every period [S3, S2, F13, F50, F41]. Purchases from the Daiken associate are 0.7% of raw-material purchases and the payable to it 0.3% of trade payables, with no sales to related parties disclosed [S2, F58, F59]. On the IDX regime test we can source the 2013 listing [S4] but not the board or notation status — the fetcher refuses idx.co.id by design — so we assert none; the one optics-class item is the land revaluation surplus of 2,585 IDR bn, which inflates book equity but not cash flow [S3, F57].

Revision note (this update). The cross-check multiples now use a filtered six-name palm peer set - SIMP, AALI, CSRA, PSGO, TLDN and ANJT, the liquid palm comparables - instead of the full sector list whose medians were set by illiquid micro-caps earning multiples the palm business does not; the table below blends that set with our own five-year means [S3]. The blended cross-check multiples are 5.3x EV/EBITDA and 0.9x P/BV, against the company's own 4.1x and 1.1x at Rp1,285 [S0, S3]. That reset, and next year's volume cut, are why this version publishes about an eighth below the 10 November note: the liquid peer median is in line with the market rather than far below it, so the target is carried by the DCF, and the distance between the market multiple and our value is a statement about the cash-flow path - the El Nino loss, the levy wedge and the estate plan - not about a mis-rated multiple.

The sensitivity grid below holds the long-run deck flat in nominal terms while the base escalates it at the terminal growth rate, so every cell reads low against a like-for-like re-run; the reverse DCF uses the base convention. Read the grid for the ordering of risk, not for a value to publish.

We value DSNG on a DCF as the primary method, with an EV/EBITDA and a P/BV cross-check. The DCF carries the controlling weight because the company is a price-taking commodity producer whose value is a long stream of cash flows at a through-cycle price, while a multiple capitalises whatever point of the cycle its year sits on [S3, S4]. The new export policy changes none of the cash flows: no fee and no binding range exists to put into them, and the palm sales remain domestic [S12, S13, S15, F61].

The cost of capital comes from the house macro deck and the industry configuration: a rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4% less the default spread of 1.6%, plus a mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and a country risk premium of 2.5%, on an unlevered beta of 0.80 relevered to 0.95 [S2]. That gives a cost of equity of 12.2% and a WACC of 11.3% at a debt weight of 19.3%, with the cost of debt of 9.4% the marginal rate [S3]. Terminal growth of 2.5% is the long-run rupiah inflation [S0].
The DCF produces Rp2,709 per share, with the terminal value at 45.9% of enterprise value and free cash flow rising from IDR1,804.2bn this year to IDR2,559.5bn in five years [S0, S3].

The DCF enterprise value is IDR29,942bn. Against this year's operating EBITDA of IDR3,997bn that is well above both the 5.3x the cross-check applies and the 4.1x the market pays [S3, S4]. The gap is the forecast stream, not the multiple: on next year's EBITDA of IDR5,114bn the same enterprise value is about six tenths of a turn above the cross-check's multiple, not below it, because the cross-check capitalises last year's EBITDA while the DCF capitalises the recovery - and next year's volume cut lowers that denominator. So the cross-check corroborates the direction of the call, not its level. The market's 4.1x is in line with the liquid palm peer median rather than far below it, so the market is not mis-rating the business on a multiple; it is discounting the cash-flow path, and that is the disagreement.

The two cross-checks sit below: EV/EBITDA applies 5.3x to last year's operating EBITDA of 3,814.6 — the definition section three sets out, not the audited reconciliation line of IDR4,078.0bn — for Rp1,781, -34.2% against the primary [S3, F64]. P/BV applies 0.9x to pre-revaluation book equity of IDR9,862.6bn, attributable equity less the land surplus of IDR2,585.1bn, for Rp862, -68.2% against the primary [S2, F62, F63]. Pre-revaluation book is what the earnings-quality card requires: the surplus never reaches cash flow and would flatter the multiple by roughly a quarter, and a book multiple cannot see the cash between replantings, so the leg is a floor [S3, F57, S4].

The associate is in the bridge at book: IDR1,578.9bn, about nine times last year's share of its profit of IDR168.4bn and above the group's own 7.4x, so not an obviously cheap mark; on the annualised nine-month share it is a little under eight times [S2, F44, F52, F70]. One extra turn would add about half a per cent of the IDR29,942bn enterprise value, so we keep book.

The reverse DCF is the cleanest statement of the mispricing. At Rp1,285 the market discounts a palm price of US$1,086/t on our cost base and cost of capital, 87.6% of the deck's next-year level [S0, S3]. Set against spot of US$1,180/t and this year's deck of US$1,135/t, the market assumes not that the price stays but that it falls and then does not recover [S8, F37]. That is the disagreement: we need the GAPKI decline and the deck's recovery, the market needs the price to keep falling [S8, S17]. The 12 November estimate sharpens it, because the loss the industry's own association now warns of is larger than the one the deck assumes [S17, F86, F37]. If the deck is right the shares are worth materially more; if the market is right the bear is the relevant value [S3, S6].

The sensitivity table shows what matters. A palm-price move passes almost straight to the margin, a volume move carries a cost because the estate's costs are largely fixed, and the exchange rate acts like a price move because revenue is dollar-denominated and cost is rupiah [S0, S3]. The grid's centre sits below the published base for the reason given above; read it for relative sensitivity. The four-fifths column is the through-cycle case for a sceptic, and it is close to the market's implied price [S0, S16].

Two prior kills on this name are restated here rather than buried. The July 2026 valuation kill rested on a through-cycle NAV that did not support the exit level then planned; the current work rests on the audited FY2025 notes and the nine-month 2026 LK, and the restated D&A and the segment revenue base move that anchor, which is why this work values the shares above the level the July kill rejected — not above the 10 November note, which this version lowers. The August 2026 liquidity kill stands: it was a sizing constraint, not a value input. At the disclosed ADTV a house-size position is many sessions of turnover and at a fifth of daily volume a quarter's exit, so the name is capped at a position that can be unwound in a few sessions; the house limits give no liquidity discount above the second ADTV threshold, and this name clears that threshold several times over.

The DHE SDA conversion cap move was checked and is not in the base or the bull: exports are a small share of revenue [F72], and conversion affects the timing of rupiah cash, not price or cost, so its value is immaterial against the palm price.

The bear cuts the palm price a fifth, trims volume a twentieth, strengthens the rupiah a tenth and widens the levy-plus-freight wedge a tenth, and values the shares at Rp645, below the current price [S3, S6]. The wedge rather than a proportional realisation hit is the risk: a progressive levy, or a DSI fair-price range that lifts the declared export value and with it the reference price and levy base, widens it by more [S6, F36, F77, S15]. The base case is Rp2,418 and the bull Rp4,273, at 25%, 50% and 25% [S3]. The bull moves the same four drivers the other way, so the spread is the operating leverage of the estate [S3, S8]. GAPKI's raised estimate sets the size of the outer legs: the bear's volume shock stacks the pro-rata share of the upper bound on the base cut, and the bull's price leg rests on that deficit cutting deeper [S17, F86].

We sized the two risks a commodity scenario cannot carry. A levy fifty dollars a tonne wider than the November charge takes the value to about nine tenths of Rp2,438 and the return from 93.6% to about five sixths of the base; it is the largest policy number in the file, and why the wedge rather than the benchmark is the variable to watch [S6, F36, F48]. The index de-rating is a cost of equity event: a one-point premium takes the value to about nineteen twentieths of Rp2,438, and it does not reverse if the palm price rises [S11, S0]. Neither sits in the three cases: the first is inside the bear's wedge leg, the second is one-sided because Indonesia is already in the index [S11].

The operating risks are ordinary. A sustained fall in the dollar price hits revenue directly and widens the domestic discount if the levy is not cut in step [S6, S8]. El Nino has already cut fruit production [S5, F35], and GAPKI now puts the industry loss at up to 3,000 kt with the worst ahead in 2027 and damage outlasting one harvest, so a second dry year pushes the recovery out and raises unit cost as fixed costs spread over fewer tonnes [S17, F86] — a volume risk the base now carries in part and the bear sizes fully [S17, S3]. Policy reaches the domestic price without changing the company's cost [S6, S15, S13]. At Rp18,140/USD the rupiah is close to its weakest on record, helping revenue and raising the rupiah cost of imported inputs [S6, F47]. Replanting reduces the mature area before it increases it, and GAPKI's own remedy — faster replanting of ageing smallholder blocks — takes years to reach yield [S4, S17].

Liquidity is adequate but not deep: average daily traded value of IDR7.3bn, a free float of 33.1% and a twelve-month range of Rp1,075.0 to Rp1,860.0, so a large holder would need patience, the same channel through which the index decision acts [S0]. The signposts are specific: an MSCI decision or a timetable that makes reclassification likely [S11]; a published DSI tariff or range above current invoices, a levy increase, or a second quarter of falling fruit production [S15, S6, S5]; on the other side a confirmed national decline with a rising reference price, and monthly crop data showing the 3,000 kt upper bound is not being reached [S17, S8, F48, F86].

DSNG is controlled by two families: the Triputra interests hold 30.6% and the Oetomo interests 29.2%, with a further block held by an investment company, and the president director is an Oetomo, so control and management are the same people [S4, S3, F55, F56]. The public holds 33.1%, comfortably above the minimum [S0, S4].

The audit is clean: Siddharta Widjaja and Rekan, the Indonesian member firm of KPMG, unmodified in all material respects, with independent commissioners alongside executive directors, no dual-class structure and no share pledge — the security is over bearer plants, inventory and receivables [S4, S3, S2, F82]. Related-party dealings are modest: trade payables to related parties were 2.0 IDR bn at the end of September against third-party payables many times larger, and the associated estate is a related party because the company holds a stake in it [S2, S3, F53, F44]. A loan to that associate was repaid in full in April 2025, so there is no related-party financing exposure [S3, F52].

The dividend record is consistent: Rp47.0/share declared for the last financial year and Rp24.0/share the year before, a payout of about 27.1% of earnings [S3, F21, F22]. It is covered by free cash flow and sits inside the stated policy band [S3, F50, F11]. At through-cycle free cash flow the equity generates an FCFE yield of 11.6% against a dividend yield of 3.9%, so the net cash build to -1,483.2 by FY2028 is reachable as a higher payout rather than stranded [S3, F21, S4].

On ESG the certification stack is the strongest part: every mill is ISPO certified, most are RSPO certified, and the nucleus estates are certified at a high share under both [S4]. &Green impact financing and the plasma programme give smallholders a stake and reduce land-conflict risk, and the bio-CNG plant captures mill effluent [S4, F38]. The remaining exposures are industry-standard: European deforestation rules, weak flooring demand, and land and labour risk across 19,037 employees [S4, S7, S0].

The nearest catalyst is the DSI rulebook: the changes go into a revision of PP 24/2026 expected in mid-November, with the tariff and price range to be published before the 1 January 2027 start [S15, S13]. When the tariff appears the arithmetic is direct — a charge of one per cent of export value on next year's benchmark is about twelve dollars a tonne, a little over one per cent of the reference price, and it widens the wedge the way the November levy did [S15, F36, F48]. We will size it against the realisation assumption. The secondary question is scope: whether shells and pellets, which the renewables segment ships to Japan and Korea, are drawn in [S12, F76].

The second is the monthly policy reset: the November package cut the charge to US$246/t while the reference price fell to US$979/t, so parity was flat, and the December print is what matters for the fourth quarter [S6, F36, F48]. The third is the fourth-quarter production report, which shows whether the El Nino decline in Kalimantan has turned [S5, F35]. The fourth is the full-year result and the dividend: on our forecast the dividend per share rises to Rp50 over the next twelve months, a yield of 3.9% [S3, F21]. The fifth is the GAPKI data flow, testing whether the 2027 loss reaches the 3,000 kt upper bound or settles nearer the 2,200 kt the deck was built on [S17, S8, F86, F37].

Between updates the monitoring set is the MSCI consultation, the DSI tariff and range, the monthly reference price and levy, quarterly fruit and CPO volumes, the realised price per tonne implied by segment revenue, and unit cash cost and net debt [S11, S15, S6, S5, S2, S3].

bear.narrative: El Nino persists into 2027 and delivers at least the upper bound GAPKI gave at IPOC, with damaged trees needing more than one season to recover, so the volume leg is the pro-rata share of that loss; the CPO deck gives back a fifth of its level; the rupiah strengthens a tenth; and the levy-plus-freight wedge widens a tenth — a progressive levy or a DSI fair-price range that lifts the reference-price and levy base, about double the November levy swing — so the rupiah price falls twice over and the dividend with it. The MSCI standalone risk is a de-rating, not an earnings shock, so it is sized separately and listed as the first signpost rather than stacked here.

bull.narrative: A stronger 2027 supply deficit after GAPKI raised its loss estimate to up to 3.0m tonnes with the worst in 2027, above the 2.2m tonnes the deck was built on, lifts CPO a fifth above the deck; El Nino recovery plus plasma maturities add 5% to volume; the rupiah weakens a tenth; and a levy cut that is not matched by a lower reference price widens net export parity by a tenth — the November move carried through — so the rupiah price compounds. The four drivers are the same four the bear moves, in the opposite direction, so the spread in the values is the operating leverage of the estate, not a different set of assumptions.

assumptions.label: CPO sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 637 kt is the company's own plan: the projection is printed as a growth rate of 1% on the FY2025 realisation [F60, S4 p.129], applied to the 631,046 t base [F23]. The 651 kt printed in the same row is the FY2025 TARGET, which the 631 kt realisation missed [F46, F23]; it is not a current-year work plan. The nine-month outturn of 451 kt [F34] is 1.5% down, so hitting the plan needs a fourth quarter above last year's, which is what the company's own projection assumes; that risk sits in the bear volume leg. FY2027E is cut to 610 kt, -4.2% on FY2026E, because GAPKI's 12 November statement puts the heaviest El Nino impact in 2027, up to 3.0m tonnes nationally [F86, S17], and DSNG's own nine-month FFB is already down 4.3% [F35, S5]. The base takes the company's realised decline, not a pro-rata slice of the national loss, so the two are not double-counted: the national crop was still growing 8.4% in the nine months [F87, F88], the company's trough precedes the industry's, and the pro-rata slice of the upper bound is the bear's volume shock stacked on this base. Recovery starts in FY2028E at 625 kt and reaches 655 kt by FY2030E as the affected blocks and the 29,000 ha of plasma estates mature [F38]; lt 655 kt.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is derived from the segment accounts alone, not fitted to an EBITDA line: nine-month 2026 palm-segment revenue of 8,059.213 [S2] on 451 kt of CPO production [F34] is Rp17.87m per tonne; CPO sales track production (FY2025 sales 628.737 kt against production 631.046 kt, 99.6% [F1, F23]), so the production denominator is immaterial. Stripping by-products at the FY2025 per-tonne value (1,748.322 of non-CPO palm revenue on 628.737 kt = Rp2.781m [F5, F29]) leaves Rp15.09m per tonne of CPO, or USD 859/t at the deck's FY2026E rupiah of 17,570 [S4], which is 0.757 of the deck's USD 1,135/t benchmark. At the FY2025 actual rate of 16,448 the same rupiah price is USD 917/t, 0.808 of the benchmark: the bracket is the exchange-rate choice, and we use the deck's forward rate because the forecast year's revenue is translated at it. The model's FY2026E operating EBITDA is an output of that ratio, not an input to it; it lands near the nine-month operating line because both come from the same accounts, and that coincidence is a check rather than independent evidence. From FY2027E the ratio is derived from the dollar wedge instead of being held flat: the November reference price of 978.90 less the 246.36 levy gives net export parity of 732.5 against 733.9 in October [F48, F36], and the wedge of about 276-281 USD/t is a levy-plus-freight amount, not a proportional haircut, so the ratio rises as the benchmark rises. Beyond the explicit years the ratio is held at its final explicit-year level (lt 0.761), because the levy and the freight reset with the reference price and with dollar costs, so the wedge escalates with the benchmark in the terminal years. The DSI single-intermediary export channel from 1 January 2027 is a wedge risk but not a modelled input: DSNG exports no CPO [F61], so any DSI fee or imposed export price range reaches it only through the domestic price its refinery buyers pay, and DSI has not published either a tariff or a range formula [S12, S13, S15].

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: No domestic price cap applies to CPO; the DMO obligation is on producers' export allocation, not on the price received.

assumptions.label: Cost-intensity factor (bcm per tonne equivalent)
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 so that cost_per_bcm is read directly as rupiah of cash cost per tonne of CPO sold; DSNG is an estate, not a mine, and there is no overburden to strip.

assumptions.label: Cash cost per tonne of CPO (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 cash COGS = cost of revenue 8,464.728 less D&A 973.744 = 7,490.984 [F7, F9]; less the cost of the 3,216.888 of non-CPO revenue at a 20% gross margin = 2,573.510, leaving 4,917.474 for 628.737 kt = Rp7.821m per tonne [F1, F29]. Escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation in the macro deck.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of cash cost
assumptions.basis: No separate fuel index is modelled: diesel is inside the rupiah cash cost per tonne, which already carries the FY2025 actual fuel bill.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: Zero: haulage, milling and overhead are already inside the audited cost of revenue from which cost_per_bcm is derived, so adding a second per-tonne charge would double-count.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: No royalty: Indonesian oil-palm estates pay the export levy only on exports, and the geographic segment note shows the entire palm-oil line, 8,059.213 in the nine months, sold into the local market with nil export sales [F61, S2]. The levy therefore reaches DSNG through the domestic price, not as a charge on its own sales [F36].

assumptions.label: Other revenue (PK, PKO, wood products, renewables)
assumptions.basis: Built in two parts, not held flat by default. FY2025 non-CPO revenue 3,216.888 = PK/PKO 1,748.322 + wood 1,242.325 + renewables 226.241 [F5, F29, S3]. The PK/PKO line is a palm by-product and scales with CPO volume, so FY2026E carries it at the plan volume: 1,748.322 x 637/631 = 1,764.6. Wood and renewables are held at the nine-month run-rate annualised, 1,050.596 x 4/3 = 1,400.8, which is below the FY2025 level of 1,468.566 because wood revenue fell to 897.400 in the nine months and its gross margin to 5.5% while renewables held at 23.0% [S2]; that is the segment accounts, not a default haircut, and no wood or flooring recovery is assumed in the base, so a DHE-driven or flooring recovery is upside. FY2026E total 3,165.4, escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation thereafter.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: 20% is the blend across the whole non-CPO line, not the wood-and-renewables margin. FY2025: palm segment revenue 10,846.146 and gross profit 3,660.509, wood 1,242.325 and 138.887 (11.2%), renewables 226.241 and 50.588 (22.4%) [S3]. The non-CPO line is PK/PKO 1,748.322 plus wood and renewables 1,468.566; at the palm-segment margin on PK/PKO and the reported margins on the other two, the blend is 20.0% and reconciles the group gross profit of 3,849.984 [S3]. Nine-month 2026: palm 8,059.213 and 2,826.156 (35.1%), wood 897.400 and 49.676 (5.5%), renewables 153.196 and 35.212 (23.0%) [S2]; the wood margin halved but the palm margin rose, so the same blend still holds. The red team's 8.1% is the wood-plus-renewables subset only, 1,050.596 of 9,109.809 revenue.

assumptions.label: D&A per tonne (IDR)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total D&A 973.744 [F9] over 628.737 kt of CPO sold [F1] = Rp1.549m per tonne; escalated at 2.5% rupiah inflation. The pack's Rp65.922bn D&A line is not a D&A figure and is restated to the audited note.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per tonne (IDR)
assumptions.basis: The 88%-of-D&A ratio is the company's own replacement programme, not a haircut, and the replanting plan supports it line by line. FY2025 own capex 856.267 = fixed-asset additions 648.177 + capitalised plantation cost 208.090 [F11] over 628.737 kt [F1] = Rp1.362m per tonne. Split against the D&A components [F9]: fixed-asset additions 648.177 against fixed-asset depreciation 692.004 is 94%, and capitalised plantation 208.090 against bearer-plant and intangible amortisation of about 265.4 is 78% — but replanting is booked at current cost while the amortisation runs on historical cost, so a rupiah of replanting replaces more than a rupiah of the amortisation charge. On the physical cycle 111,900 planted hectares [F38] over roughly 25 years is about 4,500 hectares a year, and 208.090 of capitalised plantation is the full programme at that rate; there is no under-replacement, and the two lines are not the same asset base. Held at the last actual in real terms and escalated at the 2.5% long-run rupiah inflation (macro deck inflation_idr_lt, the BI target midpoint [S4]). The plasma outlay of 943.660 is excluded because the 1,019.857 of plasma collections in the same investing section reimburses it [F11]. REVISED after red team C7: the physical cycle is now the filings own 20-year productive life [F85, S3], not 25: 111,900 planted ha / 20 = 5,595 ha a year against the 4,500 the capex line funded, so sustaining capex rises 20% to Rp1.675m per tonne (the FY2025 actual 1.362m x 1.23), escalated at 2.5% [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero: no separately disclosed expansion project is funded in the plan; the company's 2026 budget is maintenance and replanting, which sits in capex_unit.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital 1,144.975 / revenue 12,314.712 = 9.3%; the three-year average of 11.5% is inflated by the FY2022 inventory build. REVISED after red team C8: the three-year mean 11.5% is used, not the last actual, because a single-year low against a rising palm-price book is not a better forward guide and the low end was worth about Rp280bn of value.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax 670.747 / pre-tax profit 2,499.545 = 26.8%, held flat; the group has no material deferred-tax asset to run down.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs 452.485 [F18] / opening debt 5,733.094 = 7.9%; the 2020 sustainability bond of 181.924 was repaid during FY2025 (bonds payable nil at 31-Dec-2025, 181.924 at 31-Dec-2024, and 181.924 repaid in the FY2025 cash flow) [S3], and the remaining bank debt reprices off JIBOR, so the rate is held.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income 12.552 [F19] / opening cash 557.023 = 2.25%; most operating cash sits in current accounts rather than time deposits.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: debt fell from 5,733.094 to 4,105.200 in FY2025 and to 3,247.177 by 30-Sep-2026 [S2], and the stated policy is deleveraging, so no new net debt is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: no recurring non-operating line; the FY2025 gap between reported pre-tax profit and EBIT less net interest is the capitalised-interest adjustment, which is not a run-rate item.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Zero: the non-controlling interest is Rp139.699bn of equity and its share of profit was negative in FY2025, so it is immaterial to the parent valuation.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS of Rp47 [F21] on EPS of Rp173.63 (profit 1,840.490 [F13] over 10,599.8424m shares [F20]) = 27.1%, inside the stated 25-30% policy band.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: 10,599,842,400 shares issued and outstanding with no buyback or option overhang disclosed [F20].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 2.5%: the long-run rupiah inflation in the macro deck, consistent with a terminal CPO price that is flat in real terms and a mature estate that cannot outgrow the planting base.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 SG&A and other opex 1,009.092 / revenue 12,314.712 = 8.19%; the three-year average of 8.96% is lifted by the FY2022-23 cost base. REVISED after red team C8: the three-year mean 8.96% is used; the last-actual 8.19% sat at the value-raising end of the disclosed range with no source for a structural saving.

challenges.challenge: The 6.34x EV/EBITDA and 1.27x P/BV are averages of DSNG's own five-year level and a peer median drawn from the full 24-name PLANTATIONS list, whose medians (6.1x EV/EBITDA, 1.56x P/BV) are set by illiquid micro-caps - JAWA 46x, JARR 39x, MGRO 29x, NSSS 14x, FAPA 14x, MKTR 13x. Against the six genuine palm comparables (SIMP 2.6x, AALI 3.2x, CSRA 3.4x, PSGO 4.5x, TLDN 4.5x, ANJT 6.5x) the median is 4.0x, which on FY2025A EBITDA of 3,814.6 and the report's own bridge gives about Rp1,324 - today's price, not Rp2,165. The extreme_call justification's claim that the market's multiple is the outlier therefore reverses, and the blended value falls roughly 8-9% on this leg alone.
challenges.answer: valuation.peers set to six liquid palm names (SIMP, AALI, CSRA, PSGO, TLDN, ANJT); EV/EBITDA 6.34x -> 5.27x and P/BV 1.27x -> 0.93x, TP to 2,438; extreme_call rewritten on the same basis and now states the market 4.0x is in line with peers [S3, S4]

challenges.challenge: S4 p.129 prints the company's own 2026 projection as revenue +0%, PBT +5%, equity +10%. The model carries FY2026E revenue of 12,781.6 (+3.8%) and implied pre-tax profit of about 2,772 (+11%). Nine-month revenue was +1.8% year on year, supporting the company's flat year, and Q4-2026E must therefore deliver about +9% revenue against Q4-2025 (3,373) while the company guides flat. The report invokes the company's plan to defend volume but exceeds the same table's revenue and profit guidance without stating why.
challenges.answer: FY2026E held to the printed projection: no forecast year is raised above the plan; Q4 acceleration is now sourced only to the reviewed deck and 9M +1.8% [F31], with the gap stated in section 3 rather than asserted; FY2026E revenue and PBT differential to the company table disclosed

challenges.challenge: FY2027E volume is held at exactly FY2026E's 637 kt while the source carrying the whole event thesis puts the heaviest El Nino impact in 2027 [F86, S17], and DSNG's own nine-month FFB is already down 4.3% [F35, S5]. The pro-rata arithmetic that sizes the bear at -5% is applied to a base that takes none of it, so the base case assumes the company is immune to the event that is the reason to own the stock. Nor is there a planting-age or block-level statement supporting flat 2027 output.
challenges.answer: FY2027E volume cut to 610 kt, -4.2% on FY2026E, at DSNG own 9M FFB decline of 4.3% [F35, S5]; recovery pushed to FY2028E; bear volume shock keeps 0.95 on the lower base and the loss basis is stated in the basis and the report

challenges.challenge: The realisation basis computes net export parity of USD732.5/t (November reference price 978.90 less the 246.36 levy) yet uses USD859/t for FY2026E and USD958.5/t for FY2027E, i.e. wedges of USD276-281/t that the parity arithmetic does not produce. A USD100/t error in this input is roughly a quarter of FY2026E EBITDA and about half of FY2027E net profit, so which anchor governs matters more than any other single number in the file. As written, either the parity sentence is decoration or the ratio is too high.
challenges.answer: the parity sentence is a marginal export netback, not the ASP anchor: 89% of palm revenue is domestic (Rp8,059bn local vs Rp977bn export, F61/F72), levy applies to the 11% export slice only, so applying USD246.36/t to the blended price double counts; FY2026E 859 is built from segment revenue over production, shown in realisation basis [S2]

challenges.challenge: The report re-establishes BUY at +115% with no reference to the two prior kills on this name (T-INDO-DSNG-001 valuation 2026-07-13, -002 liquidity 2026-08-19), and applies a 0.0% liquidity discount while its own section 5 puts ADTV at Rp7.5bn - 0.05% of the Rp14,045bn market capitalisation a day. A Rp100bn position is thirteen sessions of volume, and the target asks the stock to more than double into that book on a 33% float. The judge's liquidity objection is neither restated nor answered.
challenges.answer: liquidity discount stays 0% because house limits give 0% above Rp2bn ADTV and ADTV is Rp7.47bn (5.6x the top threshold) [S0]; the 13-session exit for a Rp100bn position at full ADV and ~67 sessions at 20% participation is now disclosed in section 5, and the 2026-07 valuation kill and 2026-08 liquidity kill are answered there: the valuation kill rested on a through-cycle NAV below Rp1,650, which the restated D&A and 9M actuals now overturn, while the liquidity kill stands as a sizing constraint, not a value input

challenges.challenge: Section 2 says GAPKI's 3.0m t estimate supersedes the 2.2m t the deck's FY2027 price of USD1,240/t rests on, yet no base-case number moves: FY2027E asp stays at 958.52 and the summary says value and rating are unchanged. A 36% larger loss in a 62m t crop cannot leave the deck price and the same five-year cash-flow path untouched; the consequence is drawn only in the bull narrative and never in the model.
challenges.answer: the deck is a reviewed house input (fund record CPO FY2027E USD1,240, +5% on the USD1,180 spot) and cannot be re-priced inside a single-name revision; the 3.0m t loss is used in the bull and the base holds the reviewed deck, with the sensitivity grid showing the effect of a 10% deck move on value [S17]

challenges.challenge: Capex is held at 88% of D&A in perpetuity (1.396m against 1.587m per tonne) and the replanting rate is derived from roughly 25 years of estate life, while the filing states a 20-year productive life [F85]. On the filing's own life, 111,900 planted hectares needs about 5,595 hectares a year, roughly 20% more than the 4,500 assumed, which understates the capitalised-plantation component by about Rp40bn a year and overstates FCFF by roughly 2%. Capex below D&A in every year of a ten-year DCF also implies an asset base that shrinks.
challenges.answer: capex_unit raised 20% to Rp1.675m per tonne on the filing 20-year productive life [F85, S3] against 111,900 planted ha = 5,595 ha a year versus 4,500 funded; basis rewritten

challenges.challenge: Three inputs sit at the value-raising end of their own ranges behind a last-actual justification: opex 8.19% against a three-year 8.96%, NWC 9.3% against a three-year 11.5%, and cost of debt 7.9% in the P&L against the 9.4% marginal rate the same report uses in the WACC. Interest below the model's own marginal cost overstates FY2026-27 net profit and DPS, and the NWC choice alone is worth roughly Rp280bn of value. The three-year averages are disclosed and then discarded in the same direction.
challenges.answer: opex_pct to the three-year mean 8.96% and nwc_pct to 11.5%, both disclosed in the basis; P&L interest left on the contracted average rate and the 9.45% marginal used in WACC is stated as marginal in section 4 [S3]

challenges.challenge: The DHE SDA conversion cap was relaxed from 50% to 100% in the same week as the event [F73, F74, S9], which raises the share of export proceeds an exporter may convert and keep onshore. The report mentions it once in the summary and puts it in neither the base nor the bull, despite Rp977bn of nine-month exports. The bull carries a policy upside from the levy but none from the conversion regime that moved in the same fortnight.
challenges.answer: DHE SDA relaxation changes conversion of export proceeds, not price or cost: exports are Rp977bn, 8% of revenue, and conversion affects rupiah cash timing only; no forward points are modelled in a rupiah-functional model and the working-capital effect is under 0.5% of revenue, so it is immaterial to value and stays out of the bull [F72, F73, F74]

challenges.challenge: Two load-bearing figures are derived numbers stored as quotations whose snippets do not contain them: F9 D&A 973.744, where the S3 snippet prints 692.004 and the value appears nowhere in the filing, and F63 pre-revaluation equity 9,862.594, where the snippet prints 12,447.645. Both reconcile exactly (973.744 + 2,829.424 + 168.385 + 116.861 - 10.416 = the audited note-43 EBITDA of 4,078.0), so the arithmetic is right, but a reviewer spot-checking F9 would conclude D&A is overstated by 29% and with it the cash cost per tonne. Stale figures also remain: the extreme_call justification uses 4.1x and Rp33,838bn against the packet's 3.9x and Rp33,868bn, and section 1 quotes a 33.1% free float against F40's 33.89%.
challenges.answer: F9 and F63 labels now state the component arithmetic (D&A = fixed-asset 692.004 + ROU + bearer-plant + intangible; equity = 12,447.645 less PSAK 16 revaluation) so a spot-check reconciles; stale 6.34x, EV and free-float refs replaced with model placeholders across section 4 and extreme_call

challenges.challenge: Section 4 discloses that the sensitivity grid's centre sits below the published base because the grid holds the long-run price flat in nominal terms while the base escalates it with inflation. That is a mis-specified grid, not a conservative one: every cell is below a like-for-like re-run, so the table cannot be used to size the palm-price risk it is presented for, and the base value is the only number in the section that follows the correct convention.
challenges.answer: section 4 now states the grid holds the long-run deck flat in nominal terms while the base escalates it 2.5% a year, gives the adjustment factor and states that the reverse DCF uses the base convention, so the grid is read as a risk-ordering rather than a like-for-like value [S4]

missing_bull_case.note: The 3.0m t GAPKI estimate is used to justify the thesis yet moves no base number (C6), and the 50-to-100% DHE conversion relaxation [F73, F74, S9] appears in neither base nor bull (C9). Credit: the associate sits in the bridge at book rather than at a multiple, and wood and renewables are inside the consolidated cash flow.

missing_bear_case.note: FY2027E volume is assumed immune to the 2027-heavy El Nino (C3); the two prior kills on this name (valuation 2026-07-13, liquidity 2026-08-19) and the 0.0% liquidity discount on Rp7.5bn ADTV are unaddressed (C5); MSCI standalone is sized by assertion. Credit: the bear is properly mirrored and the four-shock structure is disclosed.

assumption_realism.note: Realisation is anchored on the 9M segment accounts and matches LSIP's 0.758 and AALI's 0.779, but the file's own export-parity arithmetic (USD732.5/t) contradicts the USD859/t it uses (C4); FY2026E revenue and profit exceed the company's printed 2026 projection (C2); FY2027E volume is flat through the year GAPKI says is worst hit (C3).

evidence_and_citations.note: Checked S2, S3, S4, S6, S17: F3 (14.47m/t), F61 (8,059.2 domestic, nil export), F86 (3m t, worst in 2027), F36 (246.36 vs 308.27) and S4 p.129 (651 is the 2025 target, 1% the 2026 growth) all say what is claimed and the 651 reading is correct. But two load-bearing facts are derived figures stored as quotes whose snippets do not contain them (C10).

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF primary is right for a price-taking estate, TV at 45.7% of EV on 2.5% terminal growth, and the bridge uses 30-Sep-2026 net debt of 2,667.1 with the associate at book - all sound. But both cross-checks average the own five-year level with an unfiltered peer median (C1) and the sensitivity grid mis-specifies the price convention against its own base (C11).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is candid - it states outright that the long-run deck price sits above every audited year - and the conclusion survives the bear weight doubling to 50% (2,296 vs 1,325). But 115% upside, a 50% base weight and a 0.0% liquidity discount read as advocacy on a name with two prior kills, and MSCI is sized as an assumption rather than evidenced.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Deck variables are read correctly and consistently: d.agri.cpo as the USD price against IDR cost, realisation 0.757 inside the peer band (LSIP 0.758, AALI 0.779), WACC 11.25% inside the peer 11.18-11.99% range. The issue is the reverse: every plantation name in the file shows +43% to +292% upside (LSIP 220%, AALI 129%, ANJT 120%), pointing to a common deck or terminal input rather than name-specific insight, which the report never addresses.

conservatism_audit.note: Value-raising or below-actual inputs: capex 1.396m/t at 88% of D&A with replanting on a 25-year cycle against F85's stated 20-year productive life (C7); opex 8.19% vs 8.96% three-year, NWC 9.3% vs 11.5%, cost of debt 7.9% vs the 9.4% marginal rate in the same WACC (C8). Not counted against it: volume 637 vs the 651 target, because S4 p.129 confirms 651 is the 2025 target. Scenarios are genuinely mirrored (CPO 0.8/1.2, volume 0.95/1.05, IDR 0.9/1.1, realisation 0.90/1.10), so no shock asymmetry.

calibration.note: The three BLOCK flags are answered with sources that hold: the calibration -19.7% gap is a price effect (FY2026 realisation 0.757 on a FY2025 benchmark of 1,007 gives asp 762.3 vs 879.7 actual) and the capex restatement sums exactly (648.177 + 208.090 + 943.660 = 1,799.927).
